title: The Effect of Combined Synthetic Tabular Data Generated Using CTGAN Model with Actual Data on Performance of DHF, Varicella, and COVID-19 Recognition Model
summary: Trains decision-tree classifiers to tell dengue haemorrhagic fever, varicella and COVID-19 apart from anamnesis and examination variables drawn from an Indonesian clinic's records, comparing a model trained on duplicated real data against one trained on an equal mix of real records and CTGAN output, and reading the fitted models with SHAP to rank the contributing features. RETRACTED: the publisher has replaced the title, authors and abstract on the article page with the single word Retracted and withdrawn the PDF, while Crossref still carries the original metadata and registers no retraction notice, so nothing downstream flags it. The reported results also do not hold together, which is consistent with the withdrawal: all four confusion-matrix panels report the same 85.81 percent accuracy despite very different matrices, the abstract's headline 91.98 percent figure is a single class-precision cell rather than an accuracy, and the panel it is taken from never predicts the positive class at all. The record is kept for completeness and should not be cited. It is in the index because CTGAN is the sole generator of the synthetic half of the mixed training set, with a section of the paper devoted to CTGAN's mode-specific normalization, conditional generator and training-by-sampling and Xu et al. cited throughout for them, though no implementation library is ever named.
evidence: section III is headed Conditional Generative Adversarial Network and describes CTGAN as a tabular data model proposed by reference [5], giving its novelties as mode-specific normalization, architectural changes, and addressing data imbalance by employing a conditional generator and training-by-sampling; reference [5] is Xu, Skoularidou, Cuesta-Infante and Veeramachaneni, Modeling tabular data using conditional GAN, NeurIPS 2019; the input dataset section states that dataset-B contains 5,356 records comprising real and synthetic data with proportion 50:50, set against dataset-A of 5,356 duplicated real records; the conclusion states that the CTGAN model for synthetic data can increase performance of the decision tree model but that it does not apply to all cases; no SDV or CTGAN software package is named anywhere in the paper. RETRACTION: the article page at journal.esrgroups.org/jes/article/view/2913 now returns citation_title and citation_author of Retracted with the abstract likewise replaced, and the galley PDF at /jes/article/download/2913/2309 returns 404, while the Crossref record retains the original title and has update-to null. INTERNAL CONSISTENCY: Tables III and IV print Accuracy = 85.81% on all four panels although the panels' confusion matrices differ; the abstract's 91.98% is the pred.
